correctness.rationale: Exact triangle beta integral and polynomial convolution identify the energy and all derivatives. The normalized stationary Hessian is the positive scalar multiple A^(-b-2) times the exact rational K. All nine K matrices have eight positive LDL pivots; the standalone standard-library verifier recomputes them from first principles and compares 576 entries exactly. The fixed-two-vertex gauge spans the full similarity quotient, so Taylor gives strict local minimality for all nearby strictly convex labeled hexagons. Independent 16-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature matches selected energies and Hessians numerically. No global or all-real-exponent claim.

originality.rationale: Fresh exact rational certificate proves strict local minima for all k=8,10,...,24 on eight non-similarity vertex directions. The 2023 main source only gives numerical positivity and explains that rigorous certification remains; its full theorems handle k=2,4 or the affine-image class. Accessible own records contain exact k=6 hexagon and k=6..24 pentagon but not k=8..24 for the hexagon. No checked published-finding corpus or source proves a covering theorem; hidden historical priority remains a risk.
residual_risks: A different exact proof may exist in unindexed or inaccessible sources; failed search does not prove absolute novelty.

The numerical Hessian claims in 2023 are very close as scientific observations; the claimed novelty is the rigorous finite rational proof and fully reproducible certificates, not the sign observations themselves.
No independent third-party proof audit has occurred.

value.rationale: The main 2023 polygonal Riesz study explicitly gives numerical local Hessian evidence up to even k=24 and identifies the need for rigorous certification. The regular hexagon is the first even side count for which high-exponent global symmetry breaking is known. A complete rigorous answer for all nine previously non-certified higher-even hexagonal cases is a natural finite family, covering all eight non-similarity deformation directions. It separates provable low-power local stability from possible global failure. This has scientific use independent of any unstated downstream theorem; it is not an arbitrary single-parameter increment.
